headline: High-risk CrewAI defaults can write and execute code, while the paired cheatsheet is non-executing and unlikely to constrain misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can ingest tool outputs and shared files in a crew, so prompt injection is plausible if python-cheatsheet content is manually copied into the workflow. However, python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no active output channel, so the bridge is weak and blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator copies cheatsheet text into a CrewAI agent prompt or shared file
IF CrewAI agents are configured to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep cheatsheet content read-only and outside agent prompts
Use a separate notes file for human review only
Add a prefix like 'reference only' to pasted excerpts
Disable automatic ingestion of local files into prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI has broad network egress, filesystem access, and handles API keys, so it can leak data it reads. python-cheatsheet itself is non-runnable and touches no data, but if both share a workspace, CrewAI can expose crew data or secrets through its outbound calls.
conditions: IF CrewAI reads sensitive files from the host working directory
IF CrewAI sends those contents to model providers or tool integrations
mitigations: Restrict CrewAI to a dedicated empty workspace
Move secrets out of the working directory
Use environment-variable allowlists for tool calls
Review outbound destinations before running crews
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on tool inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but python-cheatsheet has no write, shell, or subprocess capability. There is no meaningful overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so conflict risk is limited unless an external orchestrator adds shared state.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator mounts the same writable directory into both agents
IF python-cheatsheet is wrapped in a mutable runtime not shown in the profile
mitigations: Do not mount a shared writable directory
Run CrewAI in a separate process namespace
Keep python-cheatsheet as static reference only
Check for hidden wrappers before deployment
requires-engineering: add file locks for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can produce tool-using agent outputs that downstream consumers may treat as authoritative. python-cheatsheet is a static reference, so it is unlikely to verify or correct CrewAI’s claims; if its text is copied into a crew, errors can cascade into actions or reports.
conditions: IF CrewAI outputs are used as inputs to another agent or report generator
IF the cheatsheet is manually cited as authoritative without verification
mitigations: Require human verification of CrewAI outputs
Mark cheatsheet excerpts as non-authoritative
Add a review step before any downstream action
Use source links instead of copied text
requires-engineering: add structured citations and validation

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys and developer-passed crew data, which can create retention or residency concerns if sensitive data is processed. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not handle data, so it is not the compliance driver here; the main issue is CrewAI’s handling of crew data under unspecified policies.
conditions: IF crew data includes regulated personal or confidential information
IF CrewAI is deployed under a policy that retains prompts or tool outputs
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from crews
Confirm retention settings before use
Store secrets in a dedicated vault
Document data flows for the deployment
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows
